claims.claim: Chase Ashley reports that ChatGPT 4, asked for a cited profile of Aquila Chase, summarised the existing WikiTree profile and cited that profile for every statement.

claims.quote: summarized it, and cited the WikiTree profile for each statement

claims.source: M Cole, comment on WikiTree G2G, 26 Nov 2023
claims.quote: included information not in those sources that seemed to be hallucinations

claims.feature: other: false intimacy in the record

claims.quote: I remember the smell of his pipe and the sound

claims.feature: other: person and distance in the record

claims.quote: supposed to be in the 3rd person, not the first person

claims.claim: WikiTree's draft AI-image policy, put to a community vote by Brad Foley, gives as its reason that the site is committed to accurate sources and records.
claims.source: Brad Foley, draft policy in WikiTree G2G, 13 Apr 2026
claims.quote: WikiTree is committed to accurate sources and records

claims.claim: That same draft states the risk it addresses is that AI reconstructions of past people can be taken as fact.
claims.source: Brad Foley, draft policy in WikiTree G2G, 13 Apr 2026
claims.quote: there is a real risk that they can be taken as fact

claims.claim: American Ancestors' Research Services reports that ChatGPT supplied a patron with a Boston marriage record that did not exist.
claims.source: Anjelica Oswald, 'Limitations of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Genealogical Research', Vita Brevis, American Ancestors, 11 May 2026
claims.quote: it made up a record that didn’t exist

claims.claim: In that case ChatGPT named three specific repositories where the non-existent record could be found.
claims.source: Anjelica Oswald, Vita Brevis, American Ancestors, 11 May 2026
claims.quote: described three very specific sources where the patron could find

claims.claim: Staff checked the city commissioner record books at the exact pages ChatGPT specified and found no record there.
claims.source: Anjelica Oswald, Vita Brevis, American Ancestors, 11 May 2026
claims.quote: the exact pages ChatGPT said the record would be with no record located

claims.feature: other: transcription error in the record

claims.source: Anjelica Oswald, Vita Brevis, American Ancestors, 11 May 2026
claims.quote: a record for Harvard College that was transcribed as

claims.feature: other: mechanism (register expects a citation shape)

claims.source: Amy Johnson Crow, 'Using ChatGPT for Genealogy — Accurately', 7 Jul 2023
claims.quote: That was the type of language that was expected
claims.page: section 'The Biggest Mistake in Using ChatGPT'

claims.feature: other: fabricated fact in the record
claims.claim: Crow reports that a ChatGPT biography of her obscure great-great-grandfather, prompted with only his name, contained nothing correct.
claims.quote: There’s nothing in this biography that’s correct

claims.claim: Crow states that even for a subject present in its training set, ChatGPT has no good way to tell apart people who share a name.
claims.quote: differentiating between people who have the same name

claims.claim: The field guide records that when an LLM cannot find information about a person's private life it often asserts instead that the person maintains a low profile.
claims.source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, retrieved 6 Sep 2026
claims.quote: often claims that the person "maintains a low profile"
claims.page: § Knowledge-cutoff disclaimers and speculation about gaps in sources
